speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To help me understand the pattern of your symptoms, could you tell me if your double vision gets worse when you look up or down?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of ptosis/diplopia worsening with upward gaze, limb weakness that fatigues with activity and improves with rest, and the absence of sensory or balance deficits is classic for this condition. I will not request further tests as the clinical presentation is sufficient for a diagnosis.
